subject: English
central_question: How does the investigation of King Tut’s mummy show the changing relationship between archaeology, technology, historical mystery and respect for the dead?
in_scope_units: King Tut’s mummy is removed from its tomb on 5 January 2005 for a CT scan in the Valley of the Kings.
Howard Carter’s 1922 discovery reveals extraordinary funerary treasures and hardened ritual resins.
Carter’s team chisels and dismembers the mummy to separate it from the coffin and gold adornments.
The chapter contrasts treasure-centred archaeology with later X-ray and computed-tomography methods.
Tut’s family line, Akhenaten’s religious changes and Tutankhamun’s restoration provide historical context.
The Egyptian Mummy Project produces detailed cross-sectional images despite a temporary scanner failure.
The final sections address evidence, scientific intervention, tradition, language extinction, collocations, medical terms, astronomy and plants.
banned_topics: The adjacent poems The Laburnum Top and The Voice of the Rain
Later scientific findings about Tut not included in the source
A definite modern diagnosis of Tut’s cause of death
Claims that the pharaoh’s curse is established fact

known_pitfalls.claim: The CT scan solves the mystery of Tut’s death conclusively.
known_pitfalls.correction: The scan supplies detailed data and images, but the chapter does not state a conclusive cause of death.

known_pitfalls.claim: Howard Carter destroys the mummy simply out of carelessness.
known_pitfalls.correction: The text criticises the damage but also explains that hardened resins and the threat of thieves left him little choice.

known_pitfalls.claim: Tut is buried only with luxury objects.
known_pitfalls.correction: The tomb contains gold treasures as well as board games, a razor, linen garments, food and wine for the afterlife.

known_pitfalls.claim: Akhenaten and Tutankhamun promoted the same religious policy.
known_pitfalls.correction: Akhenaten elevated Aten and attacked Amun; Tutankhamun restored the old ways and changed his name accordingly.

known_pitfalls.claim: The scanner failure proves the pharaoh’s curse.
known_pitfalls.correction: Sand in a cooler fan causes the failure; the guard’s curse remark is a nervous joke.

recommended_example_progression: Begin with Understanding the Text Q1(i-iii) on repeated scrutiny, resentment of Carter and the chiselling of resins.
Use Understanding the Text Q1(iv-v) for funerary treasures and Tut’s change of name.
Use Understanding the Text Q2(i) for Akhenaten’s deeds and the restoration under Tut.
Use Understanding the Text Q2(ii-iv) for CT results, technological advances and the phrase “in death, as in life.”
Conclude with Talking About the Text, Working with Words and Things to Do on scientific intervention, traditions, collocations, medical terms, constellations and plants.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The chapter ends with Understanding the Text questions 1(i-v) and 2(i-iv), four Talking About the Text debates, Thinking About Language, two Working with Words tasks and three Things to Do activities.
